evaluation: 2025-01-15 through 2025-01-21 UTC (168hours), after 48-hour warm-up; January20 16UTC reported, never a fitting objective. January22 supplies the last uncommitted forecast day.
daily_protocol: Nine24-hour European clearing outputs; each solves48 hours with perfect one-day operational lookahead, implements the first24 and carries dispatch/online/start/shutdown history. No midnight reset. Initial online MW=min(capacity, prior saved dispatch/minimum stable fraction), with elapsed min-up/down assumed satisfied and no pending starts. Initial state is a proxy; first48 hours excluded from evaluation.
scope: Explanatory counterfactuals after inspecting 2025, not causal identification, fitted corrections or baseline promotion. Keep existing oil/CHP bids, demand, fixed hydro, original weather source and network/GSK. No new annual search.

weather_stress.meaning: Declared supply sensitivities on original available MW, all zones/window; not measured forecasts, not actual generation substituted for availability.

firm_stress.meaning: Unverified 30% thermal capacity unavailability across gas/coal groups, combined with weather/commitment; not an observed outage dataset.

parameter_status: Technology-class sensitivity assumptions, not measured European fleet parameters. Ramp/minimum-load/startup-time orders informed by Agora/Fichtner2017; startup/no-load costs and minimum up/down values are explicit experimental proxies. No tuning to583.40EUR/MWh.
commitment: Continuous online/start/shutdown MW by retained zone/technology/parent offer group. Capacity-relaxation proxy, not binary unit commitment. All monotone tranches share one group state. Startup delay, stable minimum, minimum up/down and ramp constraints apply to group totals. LP duals are conditional relaxed-dispatch prices, not a claim of EUPHEMIA pricing.
emergency: Keep original EUR10000/MWh emergency supply only as diagnostic feasibility slack; any use is reported and disqualifies the alternative as a valid supply model.
